## Intent

**Problem:** `waypoint install` currently writes only a placeholder for `AGENTS.md` (`<!-- Generated by waypoint install; content populated by Epic 4. -->`) — no agent pointed at a freshly-installed repo has any real guidance on tier rules, available commands, or where role prompts live.

**Approach:** Replace that placeholder with real, generated content: a `renderAgentsMd()` template function (mirroring this codebase's existing `renderPatchSpec`/`renderFeatureSpec`/`renderSystemPrd` pattern — an embedded TypeScript template string, not a separately-packaged file) containing three sections — tier-selection heuristics, the available CLI commands, and role-prompt locations — with `approve` deliberately absent from the commands list.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `packages/core/src/templates/agents-md.ts` (new) exports `renderAgentsMd(): string`, following the exact embedded-string-template convention already established by `renderPatchSpec`/`renderFeatureSpec`/`renderSystemPrd` — no new templating mechanism, no separately-packaged template file.
- The generated content contains exactly three sections, each clearly headed: **Tier Selection** (what Patch/Feature/System each mean and when to use which — Patch: a small, self-contained change with no design ambiguity, no approval gate; Feature: adds behavior or needs upfront design, one approval gate before implementation tasks can close; System: spans multiple architecture-level decisions, phased approval at each ledger phase boundary; tier is always named explicitly by which `new-*` command is run, never inferred from diff size), **Available Commands** (every subcommand currently registered in `program.ts` — `install`, `new-patch`, `new-feature`, `new-system`, `update`, `check-drift`, `gate`, `verify` — one line each, plain-language, no flag-level detail), and **Role Prompts** (the four `roles/*.md` paths and a one-line note on how to use them).
- `approve` is completely absent from the Available Commands list — not listed with a caveat, not mentioned as "restricted," simply never named as an available action. It's acceptable for `AGENTS.md`'s own explanatory prose to note elsewhere that a human-only approval step exists in the process, as long as no line in the Available Commands section itself points an agent at running it.
- Content is plain markdown only — headings, prose, lists — no tool-specific syntax (no Claude-Code-specific slash-command frontmatter, no XML-tag conventions, no vendor-specific markup of any kind) and no YAML frontmatter on the file itself.
- `scaffold.ts`'s existing `AGENTS_MD_PLACEHOLDER` constant and its single plan-entry line are replaced to call `renderAgentsMd()` instead — no changes to the plan-entry mechanism, the preserve-on-reinstall check, or any other part of `scaffold()`. That generic "already exists → preserved untouched" logic already covers this path; this story adds no new preserve/detection code.
- The Available Commands list is a hand-maintained static list within `agents-md.ts` (packages/core has no dependency on packages/cli, so it cannot introspect `program.ts`'s registered commands at runtime) — a doc comment notes this explicitly as a manual-sync obligation for whoever adds a new command in the future, matching this codebase's existing tolerance for a small number of independently-maintained duplicate-content spots (e.g. the `feat-`/`patch-` id-construction pattern already logged in `deferred-work.md`).

**Ask First:** none anticipated — the section structure and tier-heuristic wording are single coherent choices grounded directly in the Glossary's own tier definitions (`docs/prd.md`) and the commands actually registered in `program.ts` today, not a multi-way design fork.

**Never:**
- Add `status` to the Available Commands list — it doesn't exist as a registered command yet (Epic 5's own future story); list only what `program.ts` actually registers as of this story.
- Generate `CLAUDE.md` or any tool-specific variant — explicitly out of scope for MVP per FR9.
- Change `scaffold()`'s reinstall/preserve behavior, its plan-entry data shape, or any other scaffolded path's content.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Fresh install | No pre-existing `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` is written with `renderAgentsMd()`'s real content — three named sections present | N/A |
| Content shape | `renderAgentsMd()`'s output | Contains headings for Tier Selection / Available Commands / Role Prompts; lists `install`/`new-patch`/`new-feature`/`new-system`/`update`/`check-drift`/`gate`/`verify`; never names `approve` as an available action; lists all four `roles/*.md` paths | N/A |
| Reinstall, user-customized `AGENTS.md` | A pre-existing, hand-edited `AGENTS.md` | Preserved byte-for-byte, not regenerated (existing generic `scaffold()` behavior, unchanged by this story) | N/A |
| Reinstall, untouched `AGENTS.md` | A pre-existing `AGENTS.md` written by a prior install | Preserved byte-for-byte — same "already exists" rule applies regardless of whether the content is the placeholder, real generated content, or user-edited | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [ ] `packages/core/src/templates/agents-md.ts` -- implement `renderAgentsMd()` -- the core deliverable
- [ ] `packages/core/src/scaffold.ts` -- wire it in, replacing the placeholder
- [ ] `packages/core/src/index.ts` -- export the new symbol
- [ ] `packages/core/src/templates/agents-md.test.ts` -- unit-test every I/O matrix row
- [ ] `packages/core/src/scaffold.test.ts` -- strengthen the fresh-install `AGENTS.md` assertion

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given `waypoint install` runs, when `AGENTS.md` is generated, then it contains a section each for tier-selection heuristics, the available CLI commands, and role-prompt locations
- Given `AGENTS.md`'s content, when I inspect it, then it's plain markdown with no tool-specific syntax, readable by Claude Code, Cursor, or a human
- Given `AGENTS.md`'s action list, when I check whether `approve` is included, then it is not -- deliberately excluded from the set of actions described to agents
- Given install runs, when I check for `CLAUDE.md`, then it is not generated -- out of scope for MVP
- Given `AGENTS.md` already exists and has been user-customized, when `waypoint install` runs again, then the existing file is preserved, not regenerated over -- same preserve-on-reinstall rule as Story 1.1's scaffolded paths

Added an explicit 10s timeout to all 10 affected tests, matching this file's own existing precedent (its heaviest end-to-end test already had a 20s explicit timeout for the same reason) — confirmed stable across three consecutive full-suite runs afterward.

  - **All three lenses converged on the same real gap: nothing actually verified the hand-maintained "Available Commands" list against `program.ts`'s real registered commands.** The existing test named "lists every command currently registered in program.ts" only checked the rendered content against its own hardcoded duplicate array — never against `program.ts` itself, so a future command drift would go undetected. Fixed by adding a new test in `packages/cli/src/agents-md-wiring.test.ts` that imports both `createProgram` and `renderAgentsMd`, extracts the real registered command names, and asserts every one (except `approve`) actually appears in the rendered output — the direction `packages/core`'s own layering can't support directly, since `packages/cli` already depends on `@waypoint/core`. The original (now honestly renamed) test stays as a narrower regression guard against accidental edits to the hardcoded list.
  - **The `gate` bullet risked two related inaccuracies (adversarial).** It never mentioned the `--ci --base <ref>` mode exists, and its phrasing risked implying `waypoint install` itself sets up CI enforcement (false — that's always the consuming repo's own responsibility). Fixed by naming the `--ci --base <ref>` mode's existence (without flag-level detail, matching this story's own scope) and stating explicitly that CI wiring is the consuming repo's job.
  - **The `update` bullet omitted the exact `### ADDED` heading convention (adversarial)** an agent actually needs to write its delta correctly, unlike `program.ts`'s own more precise description. Fixed by naming the heading explicitly.
  - **`docs/architecture.md`'s source-tree sketch still showed a literal `agents-md.template` file (adversarial),** which was never built — Epic 1 settled on the embedded-TypeScript-string convention this story's own `agents-md.ts` already explains. Fixed that one line; the sketch's other, pre-existing stale entries (predating this story) were left alone and logged separately.
  - **`scaffold.test.ts`'s `AGENTS.md` assertion was tautological (adversarial)** — comparing the written file against calling `renderAgentsMd()` again, catching only a wiring bug, never a content regression, unlike the file's own neighboring `config.yaml` assertion which independently parses and checks real field values. Strengthened it to also assert the three section headings are present directly. (I also caught and fixed, during my own independent re-verification, that the first patch pass had re-introduced a whole-document `not.toContain('approve')` check here — the exact same blunt-substring fragility the review had just fixed precisely in `agents-md.test.ts` — by removing the duplicate, less-precise copy in favor of the one scoped correctly elsewhere.)
  - **The `approve`-exclusion test was a blunt whole-document substring match (adversarial)**, passing today only because "Approval"/"approved" don't literally contain "approve," but fragile to a future unrelated edit (e.g. "approving"). Fixed by scoping the assertion to just the Available Commands section's text.

## Design Notes

`docs/architecture.md`'s source-tree sketch shows a literal `agents-md.template` file under `templates/`, written before Epic 1 settled on the embedded-TypeScript-string convention every other tier template (`patch.ts`/`feature.ts`/`system.ts`) actually uses. Followed the real, established convention instead of the stale sketch -- same reconciliation precedent as Story 2.1's fix to a similar architecture/epics divergence.

The Available Commands list is necessarily hand-maintained (see Boundaries & Constraints) rather than derived from `program.ts` at runtime, since `packages/core` has no dependency on `packages/cli` in either direction that would make live introspection possible without inverting the established package layering. This is a small, accepted drift risk consistent with a few other already-logged duplicate-content spots in this codebase, not a new architectural gap this story needs to close.
